The Mountain Men (1980) Cast - Then and Now

25 July 2023 · RewindZone Archive

This article looks at the cast of the survivalist adventure The Mountain Men both then and now. Let's see how the cast changed over the years and what they got up to in their careers.

The Mountain Men is a classic 1980 motion picture set in the rugged Rocky Mountains during the early 19th century. Directed by Richard Lang and starring Charlton Heston, the film follows a fur trapper who partners with a runaway artist as they evade a Native American tribe.

Upon release, the outdoor cinematography survivalist movie received mixed reviews from critics, with some praising the action sequences, while others felt the characters were underdeveloped. However, the performers brought authenticity to the harsh way of life depicted. Let's have a look at the Cast now...

Charlton Heston as Bill Tyler - Then and Now

  • Then: Age 57 in 1980
  • Now: Deceased in 2008 at age 84

The eminent actor Charlton Heston, renowned for his portrayal of legendary characters such as Ben-Hur, for which he received an Academy Award, and his notable role in Planet of the Apes, displayed his remarkable talent once again as he embraced the part of the seasoned fur trapper, Bill Tyler. With his commanding presence and magnetic charisma, Heston infused the survivalist character with profound weight, cementing his status as a cinematic titan. The Mountain Men stands as a testament to Heston's enduring legacy. While later in his career he shifted toward politically charged dramas before retiring in 2003, he forever remains an enduring symbol of the iconic actors of Hollywood's illustrious golden age.

Brian Keith as Henry Frapp - Then and Now

Advertisement
  • Then: Age 59 in 1980
  • Now: Deceased in 1997 at age 75

Brian Keith gained widespread recognition for his notable appearances in popular TV shows like Family Affair and noteworthy films like The Parent Trap. One of his memorable portrayals was that of Henry Frapp in The Mountain Men, where he skillfully embodied the role of a lively and unconventional fur trader, contributing comedic elements to the story. Following this wilderness-themed character, he remained active in the television industry throughout the 1980s and early 1990s, frequently portraying stern paternal figures, until his untimely demise.

Victoria Racimo as Running Moon - Then and Now

  • Then: Age 37 in 1980
  • Now: Deceased in 2020 - Age 76

Portraying the daughter of Chief Heavy Eagle, Victoria Racimo is a veteran theater actress who took on occasional movie and television roles. The Mountain Men was one of her first major motion picture parts, allowing her to play a key Native American figure. Victoria Racimo was an award-winning filmmaker, writer, producer and actress. She wrote, directed and produced the recently released documentary, One Day (2015), for which she won Best Director in the Equus Film Festival in NYC.

Stephen Macht as Heavy Eagle - Then and Now

  • Then: Age 38 in 1980
  • Now: Age 81

Stephen Macht skillfully showcased his acting prowess as the esteemed Chief Heavy Eagle in the riveting film The Mountain Men. During the vibrant era of the 70s and 80s, he emerged as a promising artist, gracing the screens of popular productions such as Kojak. Macht has gracefully sustained his presence in the film and television industry, consistently captivating audiences with his performances. Notably, he has made notable appearances in contemporary series like Suits, General Hospital, and the widely adored Monsterland.

Stephen Macht portrayed the Chief Heavy Eagle in The Mountain Men. He was an up-and-coming film and television actor in the 70s and 80s, appearing in shows like Kojak. Macht continues to work regularly in movies and TV today, recently appearing in shows like Suits, General Hospital, and the cult hit Monsterland.

John Glover as Nathan Wyeth - Then and Now

  • Then: Age 36 in 1980
  • Now: Age 79

John Glover is an exceptionally talented character actor renowned for his portrayal of Nathan Wyeth in The Mountain Men. Prior to his involvement in the aforementioned series, he had already gained recognition for his notable performances in movies such as Gremlins 2. His exceptional skills as a character performer have consistently made him highly sought-after in the industry. Even at present, Glover remains actively involved in both television and film projects, showcasing his remarkable range and versatility through captivating appearances in acclaimed shows like The Good Wife, as well as in impactful movies like Pay It Forward.

Seymour Cassel as La Bont - Then and Now

Advertisement
  • Then: Age 45 in 1980
  • Now: Deceased in 2019 at age 84

Seymour Cassel had already made a name for himself as a prolific supporting actor prior to his portrayal of The Mountain Man. Throughout his career, he frequently appeared in independent productions helmed by esteemed filmmakers such as John Cassavetes and Wes Anderson. In his depiction of the weathered and boisterous trapper La Bont, Cassel imbued the character with wit and charm. He remained dedicated to acting until his passing, consistently taking on minor parts in lauded independent films and television series.

David Ackroyd as Medicine Wolf - Then and Now

  • Then: Age 40 in 1980
  • Now: Age 83

David Ackroyd portrayed the role of Medicine Wolf in The Mountain Men. He is a versatile character actor who has showcased his talent both on Broadway and in fantasy movies such as The Dark Crystal. Ackroyd's acting journey persists, primarily focusing on television roles, demonstrating his adaptability in various genres. Notable among his recent accomplishments are his appearances in The Americans and Blue Bloods, highlighting his continued dedication to the craft.

RELATED

Victor Jory as Iron Belly - Then and Now

  • Then: Age 78 in 1980
  • Now: Deceased in 1982 at age 79

Victor Jory, portraying the seasoned trapper Iron Belly, infused The Mountain Men with a distinguished aura of dignity and sagacity. His extensive and renowned tenure in the realm of theater and film included iconic masterpieces such as Gone with the Wind, as well as lending his narrative voice to the television series The Green Hornet. The Mountain Men stands as a testament to his remarkable talent, serving as one of his final contributions prior to his demise, thus concluding a remarkable and illustrious journey.

While some performers are no longer with us, it's fascinating to see where the cast of this gripping adventure movie has gone since their time together then and now.
